objects.name: OS Credential Dumping
objects.description:
Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material, normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password. Credentials can be obtained from OS caches, memory, or structures. Credentials can then be used to perform Lateral Movement and access restricted information.

Several of the tools mentioned in associated sub-techniques may be used by both adversaries and professional security testers. Additional custom tools likely exist as well.

external_references.source_name: Medium Detecting Attempts to Steal Passwords from Memory

objects.name: Potential OS Credential Dumping Activity Via Linux Auditd
objects.description: Draft Sigma rule for T1003 (OS Credential Dumping). Log source: linux/auditd (resolved from auditd syscall open; auditd syscall ptrace). Rule quality: moderate - one behavioural signal - review for noise. Derived from ATT&CK detection strategy DET0234 / analytic AN0649. Machine-generated draft - validate against real telemetry before deployment.
objects.pattern:
title: Potential OS Credential Dumping Activity Via Linux Auditd
id: a9baf8c8-0353-5bba-b1f4-5ad316cc6740
status: experimental
description: |
    Draft detection for T1003 (OS Credential Dumping), derived from ATT&CK detection strategy
    DET0234 / analytic AN0649.
    Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material,
    normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password. Credentials can be obtained from OS
    caches, memory, or structures.
    ATT&CK analytic: Processes opening /proc/*/mem or /proc/*/maps targeting credential-storing
    services like sshd or login. Behavior often includes high privilege escalation and memory
    inspection tools such as gcore or gdb.
    Generated draft - the selection values below were mined from ATT&CK and must be validated
    against real telemetry before this rule is deployed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003
    - https://attack.mitre.org/detectionstrategies/DET0234
    - https://attack.mitre.org/detectionstrategies/DET0234#AN0649
    - https://medium.com/threatpunter/detecting-attempts-to-steal-passwords-from-memory-558f16dce4ea
    - https://adsecurity.org/?p=1729
    - https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/cc228086.aspx
author: sigma-generator
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1003
logsource:
    product: linux
    service: auditd
detection:
    selection_source:
        type: SYSCALL
        syscall:
            - open
            - ptrace
    selection_indicator_path:
        name|contains:
            - /proc/*/maps
            - /proc/*/mem
    condition: selection_source and selection_indicator_path
fields:
    - type
    - syscall
    - exe
    - comm
    - key
    - auid
falsepositives:
    - 'Environment-specific tuning of TargetProcessName: Define sensitive targets (e.g., sshd, login) being memory-read.'
    - 'Environment-specific tuning of ToolProcessName: Flag use of memory dump tools like gcore, gdb, pmap.'
    - Unknown
level: medium

objects.pattern:
title: Potential OS Credential Dumping Activity Via Process Creation
id: 655246be-8eb8-5e55-999a-ca7a5457c50d
status: experimental
description: |
    Draft detection for T1003 (OS Credential Dumping), derived from ATT&CK detection strategy
    DET0234 / analytic AN0650.
    Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material,
    normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password. Credentials can be obtained from OS
    caches, memory, or structures.
    ATT&CK analytic: Unsigned processes accessing system memory or launching known credential
    scraping tools (e.g., osascript, dylib injections) to access the Keychain or sensitive memory
    regions.
    Generated draft - the selection values below were mined from ATT&CK and must be validated
    against real telemetry before this rule is deployed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003
    - https://attack.mitre.org/detectionstrategies/DET0234
    - https://attack.mitre.org/detectionstrategies/DET0234#AN0650
    - https://medium.com/threatpunter/detecting-attempts-to-steal-passwords-from-memory-558f16dce4ea
    - https://adsecurity.org/?p=1729
    - https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/cc228086.aspx
author: sigma-generator
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1003
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: macos
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - /osascript
    selection_indicator_content:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - /Library/Keychains/
    condition: selection_image and selection_indicator_content
fields:
    - Image
    - CommandLine
    - ParentImage
    - User
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative or software-deployment use of osascript
    - 'Environment-specific tuning of KeychainAccessPath: Path to watch for abnormal access, e.g., /Library/Keychains/'
    - 'Environment-specific tuning of SignedBinaryStatus: Filter out signed/trusted binaries.'
    - Unknown
level: high

objects.pattern:
title: Potential OS Credential Dumping Activity Via Process Access
id: 1744a215-6592-5beb-a33b-31accb137189
status: experimental
description: |
    Draft detection for T1003 (OS Credential Dumping), derived from ATT&CK detection strategy
    DET0234 / analytic AN0648.
    Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material,
    normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password. Credentials can be obtained from OS
    caches, memory, or structures.
    ATT&CK analytic: Processes accessing LSASS memory or SAM registry hives outside of trusted
    security tools, often followed by file creation or lateral movement. Detects unauthorized access
    to sensitive OS subsystems for credential extraction.
    Generated draft - the selection values below were mined from ATT&CK and must be validated
    against real telemetry before this rule is deployed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003
    - https://attack.mitre.org/detectionstrategies/DET0234
    - https://attack.mitre.org/detectionstrategies/DET0234#AN0648
    - https://medium.com/threatpunter/detecting-attempts-to-steal-passwords-from-memory-558f16dce4ea
    - https://adsecurity.org/?p=1729
    - https://msdn.microsoft.com/library/cc228086.aspx
author: sigma-generator
date: 2026-09-17
tags:
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.t1003
    - detection.threat-hunting
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_indicator_access:
        GrantedAccess:
            - '0x1f0fff'
    condition: selection_indicator_access
fields:
    - SourceImage
    - TargetImage
    - GrantedAccess
    - CallTrace
falsepositives:

    - 'Environment-specific tuning of TimeWindow: Define how soon access to LSASS is followed by suspicious file or registry activity.'
    - 'Environment-specific tuning of ParentProcessFilter: Allowlist known security tools or system processes accessing LSASS.'
    - Unknown
level: low
